title: What is known about 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD
description: Proof status of the six-state BB(6) holdout 1RB0RB_1LC---_0LA1LD_1RE0LC_1RF1RE_1RA0RD.
intro: Nobody knows whether this six-state, two-symbol Turing machine halts when started on a blank tape: it is one of the holdouts left open by the bbchallenge project. This page lists what has been established about it, sorted by what each result rests on.
verdict: The question is open. The passes are simple rewritings, proved in Lean for every length, but their composition produces a digit string with no visible regularity. The machine halts only if E, moving right, finds a 0 followed by another 0 (and a 1 two cells later) inside the tape; so far a 0 under E inside the tape has always had a 1 after it.

claims.title: The halting configurations
claims.text: The machine stops exactly when it reads the symbol of a halting transition (B1); the generated statement covers every configuration.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10,000 steps
claims.text: The list simulator of the shared library, proved to agree with the machine's semantics, runs 10,000 steps from blank tape without a halt, evaluated by Lean's kernel.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps
claims.text: The same run, evaluated by compiled code.

claims.title: The passes, for every length
claims.text: Going left, (11)^n C> 1 becomes C> 1 (01)^n in 2n steps; going right, D> (0101)^n becomes (1110)^n D> and E> (0101)^n becomes (1011)^n E> in 4n steps, and E crosses 1^n unchanged; each for every n and every tape around.

claims.title: No halt in the first 10<sup>9</sup> steps
claims.text: The C simulator tools/c/triage.c runs 109 steps without a halt; at the end 47,743 cells have been visited and 38,002 of them hold a 1.

claims.title: Growth shape: exp/sqrt
claims.text: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.507). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072).

claims.title: No halt in 10<sup>10</sup> steps
claims.text: tools/c/tmrun.c: 1010 steps from blank tape without a halt (122,739 ones).

claims.title: Where a halt would have to come from
claims.text: The halt is B reading a 1. B is entered only from A, which comes either from C reading 0 (then B reads the 0 that C wrote) or from F reading 0, which needs E to read 0 with a 0 next to it. In the first 2·10<sup>8</sup> steps E read a 0 about 12.5 million times; inside the tape the next cell was always 1, and the 44 times F read a 0 in 10<sup>10</sup> steps were all at the blank right end, where B then reads blank tape.

claims.title: No closed tape language from windows up to 7
claims.text: bbtools.ctl with K = 2 to 7 closes but allows a halt (12 to 1,536 abstract halting configurations); n-gram CPS (widths 3 to 7, -H, -U) fails.

claims.title: A digit string
claims.text: With the head in D at the left end, the tape reads as runs of 1 separated by single 0s, alternating 1 and 4j + 1 (j = 0, 1, 2, …; seen up to j = 8): a string of digits j. The string changes completely from one round trip to the next with no visible pattern, while the tape grows by about 2 cells per round trip on the left (square root of the steps) and very slowly on the right.

claims.title: Does it halt?
claims.text: Not known, and not reduced to a number question: the digit string is not decoded. The halting question is whether a pair 00 can ever form inside the tape ahead of a right-moving E.

claims.title: Related holdouts
claims.text: The same table as 1RB---_0RC1RD_1LA0LA_1LE0RB_1LF1LE_1LC0LD up to renaming and mirroring, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same table as 1RB1RA_1RC0RF_1RD0RD_1LE---_0LC1LF_1RA0LE up to renaming, started in another state; no common configuration in the first 10<sup>7</sup> steps of each. The same tapes at another pace, whatever the states, as 1 other holdout (listed on the explainer page).

explainer.lede: Nobody knows. Started on a blank tape, this Turing machine has run for 10<sup>9</sup> steps without stopping. This page runs the real machine in your browser, shows the shape of its run, and lists what is known, each result marked by what it rests on.

facts.text: No halt in the C simulator; 47,743 cells visited.
No halt, proved in Lean; the first 10,000 by the kernel alone.
The growth shape of the two sides of the tape (see below).

sections.heading: A string of digits that keeps being rewritten
html: Each time the head is at the left end in state D, the tape consists of runs of 1s separated by single 0s, and the runs alternate between length 1 and a length of the form 4j + 1. Here are the first run lengths at step 28,947,103 (tape width 8,068):
Read as digits j this is 0 1 1 2 1 0 0 1 2 2 1 0 2 1 1 1 1 0 0 1 2 1 …. One round trip later the string is completely different and shows no regularity.

sections.heading: Local rewritings, proved
html: The passes themselves are simple. Going left, state C turns each pair 11 into 01 (halving the ones); going right, state D turns each 0101 into 1110, state E turns each 0101 into 1011 and crosses runs of 1 unchanged. These four rules are proved in Lean for every length. What happens where one rule hands over to another, at the boundaries between runs, is what scrambles the digits.

sections.heading: Only through a double 0
html: The only halt is B reading a 1. B always follows A, and A follows either C reading a 0 (then B reads the 0 C has just written: safe) or F reading a 0, which happens only when E reads a 0 with another 0 right after it. Inside the tape this has never happened: in 2·108 steps every 0 that E read inside the tape had a 1 after it. All 44 visits of F to a 0 in 1010 steps were at the blank right end. So the machine halts if and only if, at some point, a double 0 followed two cells later by a 1 appears ahead of a right-moving E inside the tape. Whether the rewriting can produce one is not known.

sections.heading: The shape of the run
html: Left of the start, the visited part of the tape grows like the square root of the step count, the signature of a head sweeping back and forth across the whole tape and adding a cell or a few at the end of each sweep (a bouncer-like shape) (fitted exponent 0.507). Right of the start it grows like the logarithm of the step count: each new cell costs a roughly constant factor more time, the signature of a counter or of a Collatz-like map whose values are written on the tape (fitted exponent 0.072).
After 109 steps the tape spans 47,743 cells (38,175 left of the start, 176 right), with a density of 1s of 0.796.
These are measurements of one bounded run, sorted by tools/py/bbtools/triage.py; the macro structure behind them is the next thing to find.

sections.heading: Related machines
html: Other holdouts of the list of 608 that are tied to this one. The comparison of tables is exact; everything about runs was checked on the first 107 steps of each machine and is an observation, not a proof (holdouts/related.py, holdouts/related.json).

Same table as the machines below, started in another state. Renaming the states as shown turns this machine's table into the other one, the halting transition included. The other machine starts in its own state A, which is not this machine's A: its run from blank tape is the run of this table started in another state. These are different runs: in the first 107 steps of each, no configuration of this machine's run occurs in any of the others, even up to a shift of the tape. So each of these holdouts is its own halting question, and settling one does not settle another.

  • 1RB---_0RC1RD_1LA0LA_1LE0RB_1LF1LE_1LC0LD: rename A→C, B→A, C→B, D→D, E→E, F→F and exchange left and right; it is this table started in state B, in a mirror
  • 1RB0RE_1RC0RC_1LD---_0LB1LE_1RF0LD_1RA1RF: rename A→B, B→C, C→D, D→E, E→F, F→A; it is this table started in state F
  • 1RB0LF_1RC1RB_1RD0RA_1RE0RE_1LF---_0LD1LA: rename A→D, B→E, C→F, D→A, E→B, F→C; it is this table started in state D
  • 1RB1RA_1RC0RF_1RD0RD_1LE---_0LC1LF_1RA0LE: rename A→C, B→D, C→E, D→F, E→A, F→B; it is this table started in state E

Same tapes at another pace (observed, not proved). Leave the states aside and compare only the tape and the place of the head. Then a large part of the first 107 configurations of this machine are configurations of the machines below, in the same order and up to the end of the run. The steps at which they occur differ, the tables are not renamings of each other, and equal tapes with different states may be continued differently, so this does not tie the halting questions together.

  • 1RB1RC_1RC1RB_1LD0RA_1LE1LD_1LF0LC_0LA--- (in a mirror): 4,990,813 configurations, the last at step 10,000,000 here and step 6,660,591 there

summary: A bouncer on the left (2 new cells per round trip) over a tape of runs 1^(4j+1) separated by 10, which every pass rewrites (11 to 01 going left, 0101 to 1110 or 1011 going right) into a random-looking digit string; it halts only if a right-moving E ever meets two adjacent 0s inside the tape.
